Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vision.sim

Class LimelightNTPublisher

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vision.sim.LimelightNTPublisher
public class LimelightNTPublisher extends Object
Writes to NetworkTables the exact schema of keys a real Limelight publishes.

This is the piece that keeps the robot code from ever noticing it is in simulation: LimelightHelpers, Glass, OutlineViewer or a direct NT read all see the same table with the same names, units and array formats.

It also reads the keys the robot code writes towards the camera (pipeline, robot_orientation_set, fiducial_id_filters_set...) and exposes them as LimelightNTInputs, so the simulation honours them.

What this feature does not publish

The json key (the full dump LimelightHelpers.getLatestResults consumes) is out of scope for this iteration: reproducing that whole schema adds nothing the individual keys do not already give. If your robot code depends on getLatestResults, replace it with the direct getters.

    • readInputs

      public LimelightNTInputs readInputs()
      Reads the keys the robot code writes towards the camera.

      camerapose_robotspace_set is interpreted as [forward, left, up, roll, pitch, yaw] in the WPILib convention, in metres and degrees. That is the interpretation that makes the override consistent with the Transform3d you pass to SimulatedLimelight's constructor.

      Returns:
      a snapshot of the inputs.

    • publish

      public void publish(LimelightFrame frame, LimelightNTInputs inputs)
      Publishes a complete frame. Every key of a given frame is written in the same call, so a consumer never sees tv from one cycle alongside botpose from another.
      Parameters:
      frame - the already translated frame.
      inputs - the inputs read this cycle, for echoes such as getpipe.
